name: cmux.terminal.backend/1
docs: Bytes mode (ghostty-next-switch.md section 3, cloud-app.md): the backend carries raw terminal bytes; the local session host parses them, answers terminal queries unless capabilities.answers_queries, and owns snapshots and the journal. An app backend runs as the app's server (implements with server: true) and needs the restricted scope terminal:backend. No method or host op gives the backend a secret or a signature: for connection handles of kind ssh the host owns the SSH transport (it dials, checks the pinned host key and authenticates with the user's key) and the backend gets a channel (hostOps). Rust trait TerminalBackend (cmux-tui-core terminal_backend, slice S3).

props.target: string (an opaque connection handle conn_..., or a backend-defined id such as a cloud machine id; never a host name typed by a user or an agent)

methods.open: ({terminal, kind, target, open_token, cols, rows, cell_width_px?, cell_height_px?, cwd?, command?, env?}) -> {capabilities, window_bytes, resume_token?}. The session host picks terminal (it owns the journal). A kind not in options.kinds fails with denied.
methods.resume: ({terminal, resume_token, open_token}) -> {capabilities, window_bytes, offset}: output continues from offset; an offset the backend cannot serve ends with lost
methods.write: removed: input is data frames on the terminal channel (dataPlane), within the backend's in credit
methods.signal: ({terminal, signal}) -> void (capabilities.signals; signal is a name without SIG: INT, TERM, HUP, KILL, ...)

kinds.description: Target kinds this implementation serves; the registry ids are app:<app>/<kind>. Default deny: a kind not listed is never routed here.

openOps.description: Catalog ops of this app whose user runs open a connection: only an origin-user run of one of these gets an open token (stamped by the host, single use, 60 s). Every entry must be an op in the app's catalog fragment.

status: draft: shapes chosen by the ghostty-next lead (2026-10-04, revised with the SSH sample's gaps: offsets, typed host key refusal, exit signal, answers_queries, host-owned SSH transport with no signing op; 2026-10-04 later: credit-based data frames, host-picked terminal ids, denied for undeclared kinds); refined with the cmux Cloud and third-party sample backends before the interface is public

eventShapes.output: data frames on the terminal channel (dataPlane), within the session host's out credit; offset is the running total since open and continues across resume
eventShapes.exit: end {terminal, exit: {code?, signal?, core_dumped, message?}}: code when the far end sent an exit status; signal is the name without SIG; message is far-end text, at most 4 KiB, shown and never parsed

capabilities.answers_queries: bool: true only when the far end answers DA, DSR and OSC color queries itself; then the session host parses but never replies. A shell over a PTY or SSH is false.

errors.hostKey: {decision: unknown|changed, fingerprint: "SHA256:..."}: typed host key refusal; the host shows its accept sheet from these fields. Nothing reached the far shell.
errors.denied: {reason}: a kind not in options.kinds, a revoked handle, or a failed host check

hostOps.connection.channel.open: ({connection, open_token, pty: {term, cols, rows}, command?}) -> {channel, window_bytes} for a connection handle of kind ssh. The host resolves the handle, dials, checks the host key the user pinned for it (else the call fails with hostKey), authenticates with the user's credential, opens a session channel with a PTY and returns a byte channel (data in and out, window change, signal, exit status). The backend never sees the host name, the key or a signature. Data, credit and end on the channel follow dataPlane.
hostOps.open_token: issued by the host for one open or resume of one terminal after the user's gesture; host ops refuse a missing, expired or reused token

dataPlane.frames: Data moves as frames on the app host's stream (binary payload), never as op calls. Per channel, in order: data {channel, offset, bytes} (offset = running byte total after this frame, per direction), credit {channel, direction: in|out, bytes} and end {channel, exit? | lost?} (exactly once, after the last data). channel is a host channel (hostOps), a terminal (backend output and input) or a connector link.
dataPlane.credit: The receiver grants bytes; the sender keeps at most the granted, not yet acknowledged bytes in flight and never sends past them. Each direction starts with window_bytes (from the open answer, 64 KiB to 1 MiB, default 256 KiB); the receiver sends credit as it consumes data. Data past the credit is a protocol violation: the receiver ends the channel with lost {reason: "credit", retryable: false}. No frame or op waits.
dataPlane.backpressure: End to end: the session host grants output credit for a terminal only while its viewers and journal keep up; a backend grants host-channel out credit only from its own terminal credit, so a slow viewer stops the far end (SSH window) instead of growing a buffer. Input runs the other way the same way.
dataPlane.continuity: A receiver checks offsets: a gap or an overlap ends the channel with lost. resume continues the offsets of the resumed terminal.
